turns.t: Hello, doctor. I've noticed a new mole on my shoulder, and my husband insisted I get it looked at.
I'm the husband. I spotted it in the summer when she was in her swimsuit. It looked different from her other moles.
Thank you both for coming. Where exactly is it?
On the back of my left shoulder. I can't see it, so I only know what he says.
Has it changed in size or colour, according to your husband?
It's gotten bigger, I think, and darker at one edge.
It does sometimes itch a little, and once it bled when I scratched it.
Any other moles that have changed?
No, the rest are the same as always.
Have you had skin cancer, or does it run in the family? ~
Neither. My mother had lots of moles, but never cancer. ~
Any blistering sunburn in the past? ~
As a child, in the south of France. We've avoided the sun a lot more since.
What medicines are you taking, if any?
A multivitamin, a thyroid tablet, levothyroxine, 50 micrograms, and the contraceptive pill.
Any allergies to medicines or plasters?
Penicillin, when I was a baby, my mother told me I had a rash. I've avoided it since.
Noted. Any other conditions?
Underactive thyroid. That's all.
Doctor, I've taken her pulse and pressure, and weight, they're on the screen. ~
Thank you. Pulse 72, blood pressure 118 over 74, weight 66 kilograms, I see. Perfect.
Is it all right? ~
Yes. Now let me look at the mole with the dermatoscope. Please turn around. ~
Of course.
It's an irregular brown mole, about seven millimetres, with an uneven edge and two shades of colour.
Is it dangerous? ~
I can't say from looking, and I don't like the irregular edge and the change that you describe.
What should we do? ~
I'd like to remove the whole mole under local anaesthetic, and send it to the laboratory.
When? ~
My colleague will book you for two weeks' time. You'll have a small scar, and the stitches come out after a week or so.
We'll be there. ~
Keep the area covered from the sun until then, and don't scratch it.
I won't. Thank you, doctor. ~
